chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from some of his companions, from Aban, from Ibrahim ibn Umar, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
He said: 'The companions (sitters) of a man are his partners in the gift (received from him).'

key_terms.جُلَسَاءُ: companions or those who sit together (frequent visitors)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on sharing gifts with companions according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the context of *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the communal nature of social reciprocity in early Islamic society, where frequent companions (*julusa'*) were deemed partners in gifts received by the host. This principle underscores the ethical obligation of sharing blessings with those who maintain close social ties, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *silat al-rahim* (maintaining kinship/friendship) and equitable distribution of wealth within one's social circle.
